record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.original_question: For the logistic family fa(x) = a x(1 − x) on [0, 1] with parameters a ∈ [1, 4], characterize the pairs (a, b) such that every finite composition built from fa and fb exhibits the dynamic Parrondo paradox, meaning that the combined dynamics has the paradoxical complexity behavior discussed in the paper rather than behaving like the individual maps. Is the set of such parameter pairs nonempty?

evidence.quote: Parrondo’s paradox exists when the behavior of individual systems and the combined one are completely different. For discrete dynamical systems, the paradox was formulated in [4] by showing that the phenomenon “chaos+chaos=order” and “order+order=chaos” are possible when considering periodic combinations of 1-dimensional quadratic maps.
Open Problem 6.2. Characterize the set of parameters a, b ∈ [1, 4] such that any combination of maps fa and fb exhibit the Parrondo’s paradox. Is this set nonempty?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the logistic family of maps on the unit interval defined by
   f_a : [0,1] → [0,1],  f_a(x) = a x (1 − x),
for parameter values a ∈ [1, 4]. For a finite word w = (c_1, c_2, …, c_n) ∈ {a, b}^n with a, b ∈ [1,4], let F_w denote the composition
   F_w = f_{c_n} ∘ f_{c_{n−1}} ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_{c_1},
and consider its iterates (which gives a non-autonomous, periodic dynamical system obtained by alternating f_a and f_b in the pattern w).

Say that the pair (a, b) exhibits the dynamic Parrondo paradox if, for every finite word w ∈ ⋃_{n≥1} {a,b}^n that uses both letters at least once, the qualitative dynamical behavior of F_w (in terms of chaos vs. order, e.g., topological entropy or the existence of an attracting periodic orbit) differs from that of the individual maps f_a and f_b — realizing one of the regimes "order + order = chaos" or "chaos + chaos = order".

(1) Give a complete characterization of the set
   P := { (a, b) ∈ [1,4]² : (a,b) exhibits the dynamic Parrondo paradox in the above sense }.
(2) Determine whether P is nonempty.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature on Parrondo's paradox for the logistic family (Cánovas and coauthors, and subsequent surveys including a 2026 overview on chaos and Parrondo's paradox) identifies many specific parameter pairs realizing "order+order=chaos" or "chaos+chaos=order" and shows the parameter regions with such effects can have fractal structure. However, a full characterization of all pairs (a,b) ∈ [1,4]² for which every finite composition of f_a and f_b exhibits the paradox does not appear to be available; the problem is stated as an open problem and no resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Chaos and Parrondo's paradox: An overview
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Parrondo's paradox in discrete dynamical systems, including the logistic family, with open questions about characterizing parameter sets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent overview treats characterizing parameter pairs of the logistic family yielding the paradox as an unresolved direction.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Parrondo's Paradox for the Logistic Family
status_evidence.snippet: Order+order=chaos arises for observable and topological chaos; chaos+chaos=order detected only for observable chaos.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on which combinations exhibit the paradox exist, but no complete characterization of the parameter set is given.
